settings.pagination.paginate.label: Paginate long lists
settings.pagination.paginate.description: Split long lists into numbered pages with a page control, instead of one continuously-scrolling list.
settings.pagination.paginate.hint:
Changes how long lists are shown across Gubbins — the **Inventory** list, the **Activity** feed and your **Contacts**.

- **Off** (the default) — one list that loads more as you scroll.
- **On** — the list is split into fixed-size **pages**, with a page control at the foot for stepping through them.

Either way, nothing about your data changes — only how the list is presented. Set the page size below.
settings.pagination.size.label: Items per page
settings.pagination.size.description: How many items each page shows when pagination is on ({min}–{max}).
settings.pagination.size.hint:
The number of items shown on each page when **Paginate long lists** is on. You can also change it from the page control at the foot of any paginated list — it’s the same shared setting.

Range {min}–{max}.

settings.deadStock.description: How long stock must sit unmoved before it counts as dead ({min}–{max}).
settings.deadStock.hint:
How long stock must go **unmoved** before the *Dead stock* report flags it.

Only items you have opted in are reported at all — switch reporting on for an individual item, or for a location so everything stored there is covered. An individual location can also override this threshold for its own contents.

Range {min}–{max} days.

numberInput.srHint: This field accepts calculations — for example, type 500/2 and press Enter to work out the value.
numberInput.help:
**This box does maths.** Type a calculation and press **Enter** (or click away) to work out the value.

| You type | You get |
| --- | --- |
| `500/2` | `250` |
| `12*3` | `36` |
| `(2+3)*4` | `20` |
| `200*15%` | `30` |

Supports `+`, `−`, `×` (`*`), `÷` (`/`), `^` for powers, `%` (percent), and parentheses.

boot.unsupported.detailsIntro: Worth including if you report this — it records exactly what Gubbins found on this device.
boot.unsupported.insecure.title: Gubbins needs a secure connection
boot.unsupported.insecure.lede: Your browser is almost certainly capable. This page just isn’t on a secure connection, so the browser is withholding the private storage Gubbins keeps your data in.
boot.unsupported.insecure.step2: Running it on this computer? Use an address starting “http://localhost” or “http://127.0.0.1” — browsers trust those. A network address such as “http://192.168.1.10” does not count as secure, so opening Gubbins from another device on your network needs https.
boot.unsupported.scripts.title: Something is blocking part of Gubbins
boot.unsupported.scripts.lede: This browser looks perfectly capable, but one of Gubbins’ own scripts never ran — which usually means something on this device is stopping it, rather than anything being wrong with the browser.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step1: Allow scripts for this site in your content or script blocker — then reload.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step2: To check whether an extension is responsible, open Gubbins in a window with extensions turned off.
boot.unsupported.scripts.step3: Antivirus software, a VPN, or a workplace or school network can filter pages too, and would affect every browser on this device.
boot.unsupported.siteData.title: Gubbins isn’t allowed to store anything here
boot.unsupported.siteData.lede: Your browser supports Gubbins, but site data is blocked for this site. Gubbins keeps your inventory on your own device, so without it there is nowhere to put your data.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step1: Allow cookies and site data for this site in your browser’s settings, then reload.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step2: “Block all cookies”, and the strictest tracking-protection modes, also switch off the storage Gubbins needs. An exception for this site is enough — no other site is affected.
boot.unsupported.siteData.step3: Private and incognito windows restrict storage as well. Try an ordinary window.
boot.unsupported.pending.title: Preparing secure storage…
boot.unsupported.pending.lede: Gubbins is setting up the private, offline storage it keeps your data in. This happens once, on your first visit, and the page carries on by itself as soon as it’s ready.
boot.unsupported.pending.note: Still here after a few moments? Reloading usually finishes the job.
boot.unsupported.isolation.title: Gubbins can’t finish setting up storage
boot.unsupported.isolation.lede: Your browser looks capable, but the background helper that unlocks Gubbins’ private storage couldn’t start. That points at this browser’s settings or an add-on rather than the browser itself.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step1: Private and incognito windows switch background helpers off. Try an ordinary window.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step2: A content blocker or privacy extension may be blocking it — allow this site, then reload.
boot.unsupported.isolation.step3: Antivirus software, a VPN, or a workplace or school network can alter pages in a way that prevents this.
boot.unsupported.browser.title: Browser not supported
boot.unsupported.browser.lede: Everything else on this device checks out, so this really does look like the browser: it’s missing the private, secure storage Gubbins needs to keep your data safe.
boot.unsupported.browser.step1: Try the latest Chrome, Edge, or Firefox.
boot.unsupported.browser.step2: On iPhone or iPad, add Gubbins to your Home Screen first, then open it from there.
boot.multiTab.title: Already open elsewhere
boot.multiTab.lede: Gubbins is running in another tab or window.
boot.multiTab.body: Your database can only be open in one place at a time, to protect it. Close the other tab — we will switch over here automatically.
boot.multiTab.unknown.title: Gubbins can’t check for other tabs
boot.multiTab.unknown.lede: This browser couldn’t tell us whether Gubbins is open elsewhere.
boot.multiTab.unknown.body: Your database can only be open in one place at a time, to protect it — and because we can’t check right now, we’ve stopped short of opening it. Reloading often clears this. If you’re certain this is the only tab with Gubbins open, you can carry on.

dashboard.nav.tooltip.inventory:
**Inventory** — your item catalogue.

Browse, search and filter every item, adjust stock by location, scan barcodes, and manage categories, locations, batches and cycle counts.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.projects:
**Projects** — build & job workspaces.

Track each project’s bill of materials, reserve and consume stock, manage a **budget** with an expense ledger, and follow its status.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.purchaseOrders:
**Purchase orders** — procurement.

Raise and receive POs against your suppliers, handle **partial / split receipts**, and watch in-transit stock land back in inventory.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.suppliers:
**Suppliers** — who you buy from.

One canonical list behind every supplier part and purchase order. Rename a supplier once and it changes everywhere, or **merge** two spellings of the same company back into one.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.reports:
**Reports** — analytics & insight.

Stock valuation, **ABC analysis**, turnover & aging, spend over time, supplier costs and a data-hygiene checklist — all exportable to CSV.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.contacts:
**Contacts** — people & suppliers.

Your address book of suppliers and contacts, with their linked **supplier parts**, pricing and price history.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.bookings:
**Bookings** — reserve assets ahead.

Whole-day reservations of bookable items shown on a calendar, with overlap checks and one-click **convert to checkout**.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.upcoming:
**Upcoming** — your agenda.

Every date-driven event — due maintenance, expiring stock, bookings and PO deliveries — gathered into one timeline, **bucketed by when** it’s due.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.activity:
**Activity** — the global timeline.

A read-only feed of **every change across all items**, newest first, with filters by action type.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.alerts:
**Alerts** — what needs attention.

Low-stock, expiring, overdue and **budget** warnings gathered into one actionable list. The badge shows how many are active.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.sync:
**Sync** — cloud backup & devices.

Back up and restore your vault, and **sync changes between devices** so your inventory follows you.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.homeAssistant:
**Home Assistant** — voice control setup.

An interactive, step-by-step guide to ask **“where are my …?”** from Home Assistant — run the bridge, connect it, and generate an access token.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.settings:
**Settings** — preferences.

Theme, currency & locale, scanner options, low-stock thresholds, kiosk mode and the rest of the app’s behaviour.
dashboard.nav.tooltip.about:
**About** — app & storage info.

Version, storage usage, platform capabilities and project information.

inventory.barcode.hint:
The **retail barcode** (GTIN) printed on the packaging — EAN-13, UPC-A, EAN-8 or GTIN-14 — or any other code the item carries, such as a Code 128 part label or an asset tag.

Scanning a barcode fills this automatically. It is the item’s own scannable code, distinct from the **MPN** above.

> A future scan of the same code jumps straight to this item.
inventory.barcode.warning.checkDigit: This doesn’t look like a valid barcode — its check digit doesn’t match, which usually means a digit was mistyped or swapped. You can save it anyway, but a scan of the real barcode won’t find this item.
inventory.barcode.warning.length: A retail barcode has 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits. You can still save this — a scan of the same code will find this item — but it won’t be looked up as a retail product.

inventory.qr.tooLongLabels: These links are too long to fit in a QR code, so the labels would print without one. Shorten the link host in Settings.
inventory.qr.tooLongCatalogue: These links are too long to fit in a QR code, so the QR column is empty. Shorten the link host in Settings.
inventory.labels.printBlocked: Your browser blocked the print window, so nothing was sent to the printer. Allow pop-ups for this site, then press Print again.
inventory.labels.barcodeTooNarrow: This label is too narrow to print a barcode a scanner could read. Choose a wider label size, a sheet layout with wider labels, or switch to a QR code.
inventory.labels.barcodeShortenedItem: This part number is too long to print as a readable barcode, so the barcode carries a short item code instead.
inventory.labels.barcodeShortenedItems: Some part numbers are too long to print as a readable barcode at this size, so those labels carry a short item code instead.
inventory.labels.barcodeShortenedLocatio: This location's name is too long to print as a readable barcode at this size, so the barcode carries a short location code instead.
inventory.labels.qrTooSmallItems: At this size some QR codes will print too small for a phone camera to read reliably. Choose a larger label size, a sheet layout with larger labels, or show fewer lines of text.
inventory.labels.qrTooSmallLocation: At this size the QR code will print too small for a phone camera to read reliably. Choose a larger label size, a sheet layout with larger labels, or show fewer lines of text.
inventory.labels.dieCutPrinterNotice: This prints one label per page at exactly {width} × {height} mm, keeping a small safe margin clear at every edge. Set your label printer’s paper size to match. An ordinary A4 printer will scale the page up to fill its paper, or crop the edges — choose “A4 sheet (grid)” to print on ordinary paper.
inventory.labels.sheetPrinterNotice: This sheet is tiled to exact millimetres, so the print dialog must not resize it. Set the scale to 100% (or “Actual size”) rather than “Fit to page”, and leave the margins as the document sets them. Even a few percent shifts the grid further down the page — enough to walk a label off a pre-cut sticker. Print one sheet on ordinary paper first and hold it against the real sheet up to the light.
inventory.labels.codeHintLocation:
The machine-readable code printed on the label.

- **QR** — a 2-D square encoding a **deep-link to this location**, so scanning it jumps straight to the bin/shelf in Gubbins. The fastest to scan with a **phone camera**, the most forgiving of small print sizes, and the usual choice.
- **Barcode (Code 128)** — a 1-D barcode carrying the **location name** for a **laser/linear barcode scanner**; it suits existing warehouse-style hardware, but needs far more width. A name too long for the label falls back to a short code.
- **QR + barcode** prints both, for a location read by either kind of scanner.
inventory.labels.showShortCodeHint:
Print the item's **short code** — eight characters such as `A1B2C3D4` — as the last line of the label.

It is the label's **fallback identifier**: if the QR code or barcode is scuffed, torn or smudged, the short code is what still says which item the label belongs to. Type it into the scanner's entry box to open the item, exactly as scanning the code would.

**Keep it on** unless you need the room for something else — a name on its own does not identify anything once the code stops scanning.
inventory.labels.showShortCodeHintLocati:
Print the location's **short code** — eight characters such as `A1B2C3D4` — as the last line of the label.

It is the label's **fallback identifier**: if the QR code or barcode is scuffed, torn or smudged, the short code is what still says which bin or shelf the label belongs to. Type it into the scanner's entry box to jump to the location, exactly as scanning the code would.

**Keep it on** unless you need the room for something else — a name on its own does not identify anything once the code stops scanning.
inventory.labels.sheetLayoutHintIntro:
How labels **tile an A4 page**. Pick the stock you are printing onto and Gubbins lays the labels out to match it — the same columns, rows, margins and gutters — so each label lands on a sticker rather than across the gap between two.

Check the size against the packet: the sizes below are the die-cut label sizes these sheets are sold as.
inventory.labels.sheetLayoutHintCustom: Pick **Custom…** to enter the columns, rows, margins and gutters yourself.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.plain: Ordinary blank A4 paper or card, with a cut guide round each label.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-2up: Half-page labels for archive boxes, crates & bin fronts.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-4up: Quarter-page labels for parcels & large storage boxes.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-8up: Large labels for shelves, cartons & anything read across a room.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-14up: Wide labels with room for a Code 128 barcode beside a long name.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-18up: Taller version of the address label — fits a QR plus three or four lines.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-21up: The everyday address label, and the most widely stocked sheet of the lot.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-24up: Shallower address label for shelf edges & drawer fronts.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-40up: Small parts, cable flags & compact bin tags.
inventory.labels.sheetStockUse.a4-65up: Tiny component, drawer & jewellery labels — room for a QR, but only a short barcode.
inventory.labels.sheetOutlineHint:
Print a faint outline round every label, to cut along.

Keep it on for **plain paper**, where the outline is the only thing telling you where one label ends and the next begins. Turn it off for a **pre-cut sticker sheet** — the stickers are already cut, so the outline would just print a grey rectangle inside each one.

tags.empty.lead: Tags are freeform labels you stick on any item or location — fragile, on-loan, project-x. You invent them as you go, and every tag is shared across the whole inventory, so the same label means the same thing wherever you use it.
tags.empty.why.heading: Why you might want them
tags.empty.why.crossCutting: An item lives in one location, but it can carry as many tags as you like. Use a tag for anything that cuts across where things are kept: the condition something is in, who has it on loan, or the project it belongs to.
tags.empty.why.find: Filter or search by a tag to gather everything that shares it into one list, however scattered it is. Tagging a dozen things “fragile” today is what makes “show me everything fragile” answerable later.
tags.empty.why.tidy: This screen is where you tidy the whole set: rename a tag to fix a typo everywhere at once, merge two near-duplicates into one, or delete one that has outlived its use.
tags.empty.start: Add your first tag above, or type one into the Tags field of any item or location — new tags appear here automatically.

inventory.fields.inherit.custom: Set a value for this item
inventory.fields.builtInClash: Items already have a built-in {name} field. You can still use this name, but an item would then show {name} in two places, holding two different values.
inventory.fields.dueDate.label: Use as a due date
inventory.fields.dueDate.hint:
Treat this date as a **deadline**. Gubbins then raises it in **Alerts** and lists it on the **Upcoming** agenda, so a renewal, an inspection or a return-by date acts like a built-in expiry instead of just sitting on the item. Leave it off for a date that records a fact rather than a deadline, such as *Date acquired*.

The setting belongs to the field itself, so it applies everywhere that field is used — in every category, and to values inherited from a location.
inventory.fields.dueDate.saveFailed: Could not save the due-date setting.
inventory.fields.number.hint:
Optional settings for a number.

**Unit** is the symbol this number is measured in — `mm`, `V`, `kg`. It is shown beside the value wherever the value appears, so you type just the number and still read a measurement.

**Range** is the smallest and largest value allowed. Fill in either box on its own: a minimum with no maximum means *at least this*, and a maximum alone means *at most this*. Leave both empty to accept any number. A value outside the range is refused when you save the item, with a message saying why.

**Decimals** is how many decimal places the number is written to. Set `2` and `5.5` reads as `5.50` everywhere the value is shown; set `0` for whole numbers only. A value with more decimal places than this is refused when you save the item. Leave it empty to show numbers exactly as they were typed.

These belong to the field itself, so they apply everywhere that field is used — in every category, and to values inherited from a location.
inventory.fields.number.saveFailed: Could not save the number settings.
inventory.fields.number.unitTooLong: A unit can be at most {limit} characters.
inventory.fields.key.label: Key field
inventory.fields.key.hint:
Bring this field to the **front** of the list wherever it appears — on an item, on a location, and in this category's field list — so the one that matters most is not lost among the rest.

It changes the **order** only. Nothing is added, removed or renamed, and the field works exactly as before.

This is separate from **Where the custom fields go** below, which moves the whole set to a different tab: that setting chooses the room, this one chooses the seat.

The setting belongs to the field itself, so it applies everywhere that field is used — in every category, and to values inherited from a location.
inventory.fields.key.saveFailed: Could not save the key-field setting.
inventory.fields.descriptionHint:
An optional note about this field. When set, an **(i)** info badge appears beside the field on each item, showing this text — a handy place for guidance such as *where to read the value from*. Supports Markdown.

For a number's unit of measure, use the **Unit** setting rather than this note, so it can be shown beside the value.

inventory.fields.unused.title: Unused custom fields
inventory.fields.unused.hint: Custom fields are shared across every category and location, so removing one from a category keeps its definition for the others. These definitions are no longer used anywhere — no category, no location and no item — so they only clutter the “Add a field” lists. Removing one here takes nothing with it.

inventory.location.fields.intro: Details recorded about this location — a shelf's load rating, a room's humidity, an access note. Each value can also be offered to the items and locations inside.

hotkeys.enabled.label: Keyboard shortcuts
hotkeys.enabled.description: Jump straight to a screen, or open the command palette, with a single key press.
hotkeys.enabled.hint:
Lets a single key press take you somewhere — **F1** opens your Inventory, **F2** the Dashboard, and so on.

Shortcuts never fire while you are typing in a text box, or while a dialog is open, so they can't interrupt you mid-edit. Turn this **off** to hand every key back to your browser and assistive technology.

Set each shortcut individually below.

lab.title: Lab
lab.intro: Switches for behaviour that is normally decided for you. Everything here is local to this device, off or automatic by default, and changes nothing about your data — clearing your browser storage returns Gubbins to how it ships.
lab.seasonal.heading: Seasonal background garnish
lab.seasonal.intro: On a few days a year the background rain or snow carries a scattering of themed emoji. Leave an occasion on Auto to let the date decide, or force it on to see it today.
lab.seasonal.needsEffect: The garnish rides an existing effect, so pick Rain or Snow under Appearance to see it — or switch on the flag below to run it on its own.
lab.burst.heading: Effects
lab.burst.intro: Play a one-off effect on demand instead of waiting for the moment that normally triggers it.
lab.burst.label: Milestone firework
lab.burst.description: The celebration that plays the first time you add an item, or when a stock-take completes. It fills the page for a few seconds and then clears itself up.
lab.burst.fired: Fired — it should be filling the page now.
lab.burst.suppressed: Nothing will play at your current animation level: the firework is one of the showiest flourishes, so it only runs at Total Gubbage. Raise the level under Appearance, or turn off your device’s reduced-motion setting.

lab.flag.seasonal-dense.description: Spawn far more seasonal emoji than usual. The shipped garnish is deliberately sparse — a few pieces drifting past a minute — which makes it slow to eyeball. Turn this on to see the whole set at once.

lab.flag.seasonal-ignore-effect.descript: Normally the garnish only rides an already-running rain or snow layer, so it never appears on its own. This runs it with the background effect set to None.

inventory.activityLog.clear.description: Every entry recorded for “{name}” is deleted, leaving one entry saying the log was cleared, by whom and when. The item itself, its stock and everything else attached to it are untouched — but the record of how it got here cannot be brought back.
inventory.activityLog.clear.failed: That activity log could not be cleared. If storage is locked, unlock it and try again.
lab.date.heading: Pretend it is another date
lab.date.intro: Shifts what Gubbins considers “today” when deciding whether stock is dead, a batch is past its best-before, a service is due, a booking is overdue or a warranty has run out. Only judgements move — anything Gubbins writes down still gets the real time, so nothing in your data is altered.

lab.weather.heading: Snow weather
lab.weather.intro: The Snow background effect has occasional weather of its own — blizzards, squalls, sparkling diamond dust, graupel showers, warm-snow spells and (rarely) thundersnow. Normally its scheduler decides when; this forces one on demand.
lab.weather.label: Weather
lab.weather.description: Auto lets the scheduler run; Calm suppresses every event; anything else forces that event to full strength.
lab.weather.needsSnow: The background effect is not set to Snow, so there is no snow for this to drive — pick Snow under Settings → Appearance.
lab.actions.heading: Actions
lab.actions.intro: Unlike the switches above, these change your data and cannot be undone by clearing browser storage.
lab.seed.label: Add synthetic inventory
lab.seed.description: Creates a batch of made-up items so list performance, pagination and the dashboard can be tried at a realistic size. The items are obvious placeholders and are added to your real inventory.
lab.seed.confirmBody: This writes {count} made-up items into your inventory. They are named so they are easy to spot and delete afterwards, but this cannot be undone by clearing browser storage.
lab.flag.pwa-update-available.label: Pretend an update is waiting
lab.flag.pwa-update-available.descriptio: Shows the “a new version is ready” prompt without deploying anything. The incoming build is reported as sharing this build’s data format, so the prompt takes its reassuring path.
lab.flag.pwa-update-breaking.label: Pretend the waiting update changes the data format
lab.flag.pwa-update-breaking.description: Reports the pretend update as using a newer data format, so the prompt shows its data-safety warning instead. Needs the flag above to be on.
lab.flag.force-large-format.label: Force the large-format layout
lab.flag.force-large-format.description: The tablet layout needs both a large window and a touch screen, so a desktop can never show it. This forces it on regardless of the device.
lab.flag.no-camera.label: Pretend there is no camera
lab.flag.no-camera.description: Makes the barcode scanner behave as though the device has no usable camera, so its fallback and error copy can be checked on a machine that does have one.
lab.flag.storage-persistence-denied.desc: Shows the “your data may be cleared by the browser” state even where the browser has already granted persistence.
lab.flag.force-offline.label: Pretend to be offline
lab.flag.force-offline.description: Reports the app as offline without touching your real connection, so offline banners and the queued-sync paths can be checked on demand.
lab.flag.schema-too-new.label: Pretend the local database is from a newer version
lab.flag.schema-too-new.description: Triggers the “this database was written by a newer Gubbins” screen, which normally only appears after opening an older build against a migrated database. Nothing on disk is actually changed.
lab.flag.sync-lww-tie.label: Force a sync timestamp tie
lab.flag.sync-lww-tie.description: Makes incoming rows arrive carrying exactly the local row’s timestamp, reproducing the tie that last-write-wins has to break. Useful when investigating devices that keep re-syncing the same rows.

The supplier's product page — paste the full `https://…` link.

With the companion browser extension installed, a **re-scrape** reads live price, order code and other details straight from this page, matching the supplier by the link's host. scraping.panel.urlHint:
Paste the **product page** link from a distributor Gubbins has a scraper for: **{suppliers}**.

Anything else is refused before it is fetched — Gubbins only reaches the distributors it can actually read. For an Amazon listing, use the extension's toolbar button on the tab you already have open instead of pasting the link here.

The distributor or shop you buy from. Pick one you already use from the list, or simply **type a new name** — it is added to your suppliers when you save.

suppliers.intro: Suppliers are the companies you buy from — the same record sits behind every supplier part and every purchase order. Tidy the whole list here: correct a name once and it changes everywhere, fold two spellings of the same company into one, or remove one you no longer use.

events.itemCreated.description: A new item was added — including a new variant, or one assembled from a kit.
events.itemRenamed.label: Item renamed
events.itemRenamed.description: An existing item was given a different name.
events.itemRemoved.label: Item removed

events.itemRestored.label: Item restored
events.itemRestored.description: An archived item was brought back into the active inventory.
events.itemChanged.label: Item changed
events.itemChanged.description: A change with no more specific event of its own — a revaluation, a test record, or a loan renewal. Also covers changes made by a newer version of Gubbins that this one does not recognise.
events.stockAdjusted.label: Stock adjusted
events.stockAdjusted.description: The amount on hand changed for any reason — counted, consumed, received, sold, written off, or returned to a supplier.
events.lowStock.label: Stock ran low
events.lowStock.description: A stock movement left an item at or below its reorder point. Fires alongside the movement itself, not instead of it.
events.outOfStock.label: Stock ran out
events.outOfStock.description: A stock movement left an item with nothing on hand. Sent instead of "Stock ran low", never as well as it.
events.itemMoved.label: Item moved
events.itemMoved.description: An item was moved to a different location, or its location was re-parented.
events.locationCreated.label: Location created
events.locationCreated.description: A new storage location was added — a room, a shelf, a drawer, a box.
events.locationRenamed.label: Location renamed
events.locationRenamed.description: A storage location was given a different name. Nothing stored in it moved.
events.locationMoved.label: Location moved
events.locationMoved.description: A storage location was moved under a different parent, or out to the top level. Everything nested inside it went with it.
events.locationArchived.label: Location archived
events.locationArchived.description: A storage location was hidden from the tree and the pickers. Nothing stored in it moved, and it can be restored.
events.locationRestored.label: Location restored
events.locationRestored.description: An archived storage location was brought back into the hierarchy.
events.locationRemoved.label: Location deleted
events.locationRemoved.description: A storage location was deleted. Anything stored in it moved to Unassigned and any sub-locations were promoted to its parent.
events.locationChanged.label: Location changed
events.locationChanged.description: A change to a storage location with no more specific event of its own — including changes made by a newer version of Gubbins that this one does not recognise.
events.itemCheckedOut.label: Item checked out
events.itemCheckedOut.description: An item was lent out or taken by someone.
events.itemCheckedIn.label: Item checked in
events.itemReserved.label: Item reserved
events.itemReserved.description: An item was set aside for a project or a job.
events.itemReservationCleared.label: Reservation cleared
events.itemReservationCleared.descriptio: A reservation was released and the item is available again.
events.itemConditionChanged.label: Condition changed
events.itemConditionChanged.description: An item's recorded condition was updated.
events.itemMaintenanceLogged.label: Maintenance logged

inventory.location.hint.nameCreate:
The location's display name — e.g. **Workshop**, **Cabinet A**, **Drawer 3**. It appears throughout Gubbins: the location tree, item lists, pickers and printed labels. The text is tinted with the colour you pick below.

Use a **`/`** (or **`\`**) to create several nested levels at once: typing **`Workshop/Cabinet A/Drawer 3`** makes *Drawer 3* inside *Cabinet A* inside *Workshop*. Any level that already exists is reused rather than duplicated, so only the missing ones are added.

Use a **comma** to add several locations side by side at the last level: **`Garage/Box 1, Box 2, Box 3`** makes *Box 1*, *Box 2* and *Box 3* as siblings inside *Garage*. They each take the icon, colour and capacity you set below.

Need a comma **in** a name? Type it twice — **`Bay 1,, 2`** creates a single location called *Bay 1, 2*.
inventory.location.hint.parent: Nest this location inside another to build your storage hierarchy (Building → Room → Cabinet → Drawer). Leave as **Top level** for a root location. You can re-parent it later; a location can't be moved inside itself or one of its own children.
inventory.location.hint.description: An optional note about what lives here, for your own reference. It rides as a tooltip on the location in the tree and shows in its Edit panel.
inventory.location.hint.icon: The **icon** shown for this location in the tree and in the details panel above the item list, so you can recognise it at a glance. Pick any glyph you like — a cabinet, a shelf, a car, a plant. Optional — locations without an icon use a plain folder.
inventory.location.hint.colour: An optional tint applied to this location's **name** everywhere it appears — the tree, pickers and labels — so it stands out. Purely visual; it changes no behaviour.
inventory.location.hint.capacity: An optional limit on how many items this location should hold. When set, Gubbins shows a **fullness gauge** and warns you when you add an item to a full location. Leave blank for no limit.
inventory.location.hint.dimensions:
The location's **internal** width, height and depth — the usable space inside, in your chosen dimension unit (change the unit in **Settings**). Enter all three and Gubbins works out the **volume** shown just below.

Sizes are stored independently of the unit, so switching units just re-displays the same measurements — nothing is converted or lost. Leave them blank if you don't measure this location.
inventory.location.hint.usableVolume:
Optional **override** for the usable volume inside this location, for a container that isn’t a neat box — a bag, a bin with sloped walls, a shelf with a lip. When set, Gubbins uses this figure for **space used** instead of multiplying the width × height × depth above.

Leave it blank to just use the box measurements.
inventory.location.hint.packingFactor:
Optional **packing efficiency** for this location — the share of its volume that’s realistically fillable, since rigid items leave gaps and you can’t pack to 100%. A lower value gives a more conservative **space used** reading.

Leave it blank to use the global default from **Settings → Appearance**.
inventory.location.hint.deadStockMode:
Whether items stored here are flagged on the **Dead stock** report once they go unused — a handy way to watch a whole cupboard without setting each item individually.

- **Inherit** — follow the location above; if nothing above opts in, items here are not reported.
- **Report** — flag items stored here (and in its sub-locations) once they go unmoved.
- **Ignore** — never flag items here, even if a location above reports everything.

An individual item can always override this from its own **Dead-stock reporting** panel.
inventory.location.hint.deadStockDays:
How long items stored here must sit unmoved before they count as dead stock. Leave blank to use the value from the location above, or the global default in **Settings → Inventory → Stock alerts & lifecycle**.

Useful when one place keeps different time to the rest: deep storage might only be worth flagging after a year, while a workbench goes stale in a month.
inventory.location.hint.default: Pre-select this location when adding a new item, so your most-used spot is one click away. Only **one** location can be the default; choosing this clears it from any other.
inventory.location.hint.walkOrder:
Where this location sits on your **picking route** — the order you naturally walk past it when gathering parts (by the door might be **1**, the far shelving **9**). When you pick a project's parts, the **Picking** worksheet lists everything in this order so you gather it in one sweep instead of doubling back.

Lower numbers come first; ties fall back to the usual busiest-location order. Leave blank to leave this location off the route — it then sorts after the places you have ordered.

users.subject.items.help:
Everything in the catalogue — the item records themselves and everything attached to them.

- **View** opens the Inventory screen, item search, the command palette's item results and every item page. Without it, a deep link to an item is refused too.
- **Change** covers an item's own details *and* the things attached to it: attachments, photos, tags, capabilities, kits, variants, test records and BOM lines.
- **Delete** removes the item itself, and permits the *All items* danger-zone entry.

How much of something there is lives under **Stock levels**, not here.
users.subject.stock.help:
Quantities, batches, gauges and cycle counts — how much of something there is, as opposed to what it is.

- **View** is granted for completeness; nothing in the app checks it yet, because a quantity is read wherever its item is shown.
- **Change** covers adjusting a quantity, moving stock between locations, receiving against a purchase order, reading a gauge and running a cycle count.

There is no **Delete**. Stock is written down to zero or written off, never deleted.
users.subject.locations.help:
Places things live — the location tree, its photos and its marked-up regions.

- **View** gates the bridge's location endpoints. Inside the app a location is shown wherever an item names it, so the app itself does not check it.
- **Change** covers creating, renaming, moving and archiving locations, and their photos and regions.
- **Delete** removes a location outright.
users.subject.categories.help:
Categories, and the custom fields they define.

- **View** gates the bridge's category endpoints; the app shows a category wherever an item names one.
- **Change** covers the category tree *and* the custom-field definitions beneath it — adding a field changes what every item in that category records.
- **Delete** removes a category.
users.subject.tags.help:
Tags, and which items and locations carry them.

- **View** opens the Tags screen.
- **Change** creates and renames tags. Putting a tag *on* an item needs **Items → Change**, not this.
- **Delete** removes a tag from everything holding it.
users.subject.projects.help:
Projects, their budgets, and the assemblies built under them.

- **View** opens the Projects screen and the Dashboard's project and budget cards.
- **Change** covers project details, budgets, and committing or drawing items into an assembly.
- **Delete** removes a project.
users.subject.contacts.help:
People and organisations — borrowers, and whoever a booking or a loan is raised against.

- **View** opens the Contacts screen.
- **Change** creates and edits a contact.
- **Delete** removes one.
users.subject.suppliers.help:
Suppliers, and their part catalogues.

- **View** opens the Suppliers screen.
- **Change** covers supplier details and the supplier parts, prices and lead times beneath them.
- **Delete** removes a supplier and its parts.
users.subject.purchase-orders.help:
Purchase orders, from raising one to receiving it.

- **View** opens the Purchase orders screen and the Dashboard's in-transit card.
- **Change** raises and edits an order, and receives a delivery against it. Receiving also writes stock, so it needs **Stock levels → Change** as well.
- **Delete** removes an order.
users.subject.bookings.help:
Reservations of equipment for a future date.

- **View** opens the Bookings screen, the Upcoming agenda's booking entries and the bridge's calendar feed.
- **Change** creates and edits a booking.
- **Delete** cancels one outright.
users.subject.checkouts.help:
Loans — equipment signed out to someone, and signed back in.

- **View** opens the Dashboard’s overdue card and the Upcoming agenda’s loan entries. Loans have no screen of their own.
- **Change** checks an item out and back in, in the app and over the bridge. Returning something is a Change, not a delete.
- **Delete** erases the loan *ledger*: the **Loans** entry in the danger zone, and the loans that go with an item when it is deleted. There is no per-loan delete — an individual loan is closed by checking it in.
users.subject.maintenance.help:
Servicing an asset — schedules, due dates and completed jobs.

- **View** opens the Dashboard's maintenance card and the Alerts entries drawn from it. Maintenance has no screen of its own.
- **Change** creates a schedule and records a job as done.
- **Delete** removes a schedule and its history.

This is servicing *assets*. Housekeeping the database itself is **Storage**.
users.subject.wishlist.help:
Things you intend to acquire but do not yet hold.

- **View** is granted for completeness; nothing checks it yet.
- **Change** adds and edits a wishlist entry.
- **Delete** removes one.
users.subject.reports.help:
The Reports screen, the printable catalogue and the insurance schedule.

- **View** opens all three, and the command palette's entries for them.

A report is drawn from the data other permissions govern, so it shows only what its figures come from. There is nothing here to change or delete.
users.subject.audit.help:
The activity history — the record of who changed what, and when.

- **View** opens the Activity screen, the per-item and per-location history tabs, the Dashboard's recent-activity card and the bridge's activity feeds.
- **Delete** prunes the ledger: retention sweeps, and clearing a single item's log.

There is no **Change**. The ledger records what happened; it is pruned, never edited.
users.subject.import.help:
Bringing records in from a file or a supplier catalogue, in bulk.

- **Run** opens the Import screen and the import dialog, and lets a merge commit.

An import also writes the records it creates, so it needs the **Change** permission for every area it touches — an item import needs **Items → Change** as well. This permission is the separate question of whether someone may do it *in bulk*: merging thousands of rows is not the same act as editing one.
users.subject.export.help:
Taking data out — the export wizard, the vault archive, and the CSV and spreadsheet buttons on Activity, Alerts, Bookings, Contacts and the location lists.

- **Run** permits all of them.

> Withholding this hides nothing on screen. Someone with **Items → View** still reads every item; this decides only whether they can take the lot away in one file.
users.subject.labels.help:
Printing — item labels, location labels and QR codes.

- **Print** opens the label and QR dialogs.

Printing reads the details it puts on the label, so it also needs **Items → View** or **Locations → View** for whatever is being printed.
users.subject.settings.help:
This device’s own preferences — appearance, language, notifications, scanning and hotkeys.

- **View** does not gate the Settings screen, which deliberately stays open to everyone: it holds this device’s preferences rather than your inventory. It does gate the bridge’s webhook delivery log.
- **Change** is what bites in the app: it governs the danger-zone entries that reset app and device settings.

Data housekeeping is **Storage**; which features exist at all is **Modules**.
users.subject.modules.help:
The Modules screen, which decides which parts of Gubbins exist on this device.

- **View** opens the screen.
- **Change** applies a preset, resets the layout, and switches an individual module on or off.

> **Change here protects every other permission.** Switching the Users module off takes the sign-in gate down with it, so whoever holds this can hand themselves everything. The built-in **Manager** role is deliberately given View without Change for that reason.

Grant **View** alongside it. **Change** on its own does not open the screen, so a role holding only Change can edit nothing.
users.subject.storage.help:
Housekeeping the database on this device, as opposed to the records inside it.

- **View** shows storage usage, row counts and the diagnostics figures.
- **Change** compacts the database, sweeps orphaned images, downgrades stored photos, and covers the developer lab's data seeding and clock override.

This is not **Maintenance**, which means servicing an asset. Pruning the activity history is **Activity history → Delete**.
users.subject.users.help:
Accounts and roles.

- **View** opens the Users screen and lists the accounts and roles on it.
- **Manage** creates, edits, disables and deletes accounts, sets and clears passwords, mints and revokes API tokens, and creates, edits and deletes roles.

There is no separate Delete: anyone who can edit an account can assign themselves any role, so splitting the two would be a distinction without a difference. An API token is always held to the role of the account it was minted against.
users.subject.backup.help:
Backup files — a copy of the whole database.

- **View** permits *creating* a backup. A backup is a copy of everything rather than a page to look at, which is why creating one sits under View.
- **Change** permits *restoring* one.

> **Change is powerful.** A restore rewrites every synced record from the file, and accounts and roles are synced records — so someone who can restore can, with a hand-edited backup, change what any account is allowed to do.

Backup and restore share the Sync screen, so that screen opens for a role granted backups even without **Sync → View**, and shows only the backup half to it.
users.subject.sync.help:
Keeping devices in step through a cloud folder.

- **View** opens the Sync screen and shows the link's status.
- **Change** signs in to the cloud provider, links and unlinks a folder, runs a sync, resets the remote copy, and applies what arrives from another device.
users.subject.bridge.help:
The bridge — the local service that serves Gubbins to Home Assistant, MCP clients and other tools.

- **View** opens the Webhooks and Home Assistant screens.
- **Change** sets the bridge token, and edits and test-fires webhooks.

A bridge request is checked against the role of the account its API token belongs to *and* against this permission, so the bridge can be withheld from a role that otherwise has full access in the app.
users.slot.view.help:
**View** decides whether someone may *see* an area.

For most areas it is the screen gate: take it away and the screen disappears from the navigation menu, the Dashboard, the keyboard shortcuts and the command palette, and typing its address lands on a short refusal instead.

It is not per-record visibility. A screen someone can open shows **everything** on it — Gubbins has no concept of hiding one item from one person. Information also travels between areas by design: an item's page names its project and its supplier whether or not that person can open those screens.
users.slot.change.help:
**Change** decides whether someone may *create or edit* in an area.

It covers the thing itself **and** what is attached to it — an item's attachments, photos, tags and BOM lines are all part of changing the item. It never implies **Delete**.

A few areas name this column differently, because the word is narrower there: **Manage** for accounts and roles, **Run** for import and export, **Print** for labels. Each box does exactly what its own caption says.
users.slot.delete.help:
**Delete** decides whether someone may *remove* records outright.

It is always separate from **Change**, and never granted by it — the built-in **Stocker** role can edit any item and delete none.

It also governs the danger zone: erasing all of an area needs that area's Delete, and an entry that takes other records with it needs *their* Delete too. Some areas have no Delete at all — stock is written down rather than deleted, and the activity history is pruned rather than edited.

category.lookupSources.title: Fill from an open database
category.lookupSources.blurb: Let items in this category be filled in from a free, open database — you pick the right match and review every value first.
category.lookupSources.hint:
Some things are already described in a public database, so there is no need to retype what someone has already written down.

Tick a database here and every item in this category gains a **Fill from a database** button. It searches by the item’s name, asks you **which** entry is the right one, then shows you exactly what it would put where — **your own entries are never overwritten** unless you tick them.

Nothing is sent anywhere until you press the button, and the first time you use one you are asked to agree to that database’s address. You can withdraw that agreement later under **Settings → Scanning & labels**.

settings.lookupConsent.label: Sites you’ve agreed to
settings.lookupConsent.description: The open databases this device may contact when you fill an item’s fields from one. Remove any to be asked again.
settings.lookupConsent.hint:
A category can be set up to **fill an item’s fields from an open database**. Before this device contacts one for the first time, Gubbins asks your permission and names the exact site.

Each site is agreed to **separately** — saying yes to a film database is not saying yes to everything — and only the item’s name is ever sent, only when you press the button.

Removing a site here **withdraws** that agreement: nothing is contacted until you agree again. This choice stays on **this device**: it is never shared by settings sync, and a backup only restores it if you include the *This device* group.

scraping.extension.description.behind: Version {version} speaks protocol generation {protocol}; this app speaks {current}. Rebuild the extension and reload it to get the newer capabilities.
scraping.extension.hint:
The **companion browser extension** fetches supplier pages, barcodes and open-database records on the app’s behalf.

The app and the extension are updated separately, so they can end up a generation apart. Each announces the **protocol generation** it speaks, and a capability is offered only when the extension actually understands it — so a barcode lookup uses the app’s own online lookup (asking you first) instead of waiting on an extension that would ignore it.

Quote the version here if you ever report a problem with scraping or lookups.
